notes.heading:null: means any non-empty heading is acceptable. Use it for a page whose title is DATA-DRIVEN, so the baseline does not go red the day the data changes. It still fails on an error boundary, on a missing heading and on a wrong status.
notes.maxBytes: An absolute byte ceiling, set by a person and never written or raised by --update-baseline. A ceiling a machine can raise is not a ceiling. Set ONLY on routes whose shape is settled. /monopoly 5,000,000: bounded at 500 rows by wire-bound.ts with candidates claiming the budget first, so its shape cannot grow with the catalogue; measured 3,821,977, ~24% headroom. DELIBERATELY ABSENT on /suppliers (8,027,605) and /pricing (5,453,717): both are about to change shape under a bounded server-side projection, and a ceiling pinned to a number about to drop would either bless today's size forever or fail the promote that improves it. ALSO ABSENT ON /board, and this one was SET AND THEN WITHDRAWN THE SAME MINUTE, which is worth recording. 5,500,000 looked right against today's 4,639,897 and the 80% warning fired at 84% immediately. Checking why exposed the real fact: /board is bounded per feed day but the feed day is not bounded. The archive holds days from 231 to 5,488 index rows; at the measured 1,682 bytes/row a heavy Monday is roughly 9.2 MB. The ceiling would have passed all week and failed on a legitimately large government file, blaming whoever promoted that morning. A gate that fires on real data is worse than no gate, because it teaches everyone to override it. /board needs a BOUND before it can take a CEILING, exactly like the other two. The 80%-headroom warning caught this within seconds of the ceiling being written, which is the clearest argument for warning-while-passing over a bare cliff.
